name: The Spire Looks Down: An Unauthorized Interior
creator: Published anonymously; attributed by literary detectives to 'Nneka S.' (identity disputed)
description: A novel written from the interior perspective of a Tier 5 Spire resident over the course of a single year, depicting in granular and apparently intimate detail the social rituals, consumption habits, romantic intrigues, and casual brutalities of the ultra-elite — including what they say about lower tiers when they believe no one is listening. The prose is deliberately flat and affectless, which amplifies rather than mutes the horror. It was uploaded anonymously to a gray-market neural feed channel in 2218 and has never been officially published.
medium: neural feed only (anonymous upload; multiple mirrors; no physical edition exists)
cultural_impact: Caused a genuine crisis of paranoia in Spire social circles upon release, as multiple characters were recognized as thinly veiled portraits of real individuals; it remains the most-discussed piece of underground literature in Meridian 88 and the subject of at least three academic analyses.
controversy: Several Tier 5 families have filed civil actions against unnamed parties, which have all stalled due to the author's anonymity. The novel contains details that could only be known by someone with genuine Spire access, leading to ongoing speculation. At least two people have been wrongly identified as the author, with serious consequences for their lives.
story_hooks: One of the wrongly identified authors is now being actively persecuted by a Tier 5 family and needs help proving they didn't write the book — which means finding evidence of who actually did.
A newly uploaded chapter appeared on the mirrors six months ago, extending the story into 2223 — meaning the author is still active, still with Spire access, and still watching.

A specific scene in the novel describes, in passing, a transaction that is actually evidence of a serious crime — the kind of crime that would destabilize multiple corponation governance structures if it became actionable.
